home.name: The Arcaneum
home.heroBody: The College of Winterhold's own library, every tome shelved and waiting. Pick a tool to get started—everything here works on collections you've already installed in Vortex: mend them faster, ward your Ignored and Disabled mods through an update, transcribe conflict rules, and see how it all went.
home.cardDesc: Every tool in the collection, shelved and waiting.

merge.name: The Forge
merge.heroBody: Every forge fuses raw ore into a single, stronger blade. Pick plugins from one or more collections and The Forge bundles them into one file—freeing up load-order slots without ever touching xEdit yourself. Review exactly what's going in before you strike, and it'll flag the result as ESL automatically when it fits.
merge.cardDesc: Forge many plugins into one—reclaim load-order slots and stay clear of the 254-plugin limit.

rebuild.name: Restoration
rebuild.heroBody: Restoration magic mends the broken back to full health in moments, not seasons. This tool re-extracts an already-installed collection's mods directly into your staging folder—same result as Vortex's own install, dramatically faster. Review exactly what would change before you cast it, then let the spell run while you do something else.
rebuild.cardDesc: Mends broken and corrupted files in seconds—skip the slow journey of a full reinstall.

sync.name: The Herald
sync.heroBody: A Herald announces what's coming before it arrives — and makes sure nothing you've already chosen gets undone along the way. Updating a collection in Vortex often resets your carefully-set Ignored and Disabled mods back to their defaults—this tool remembers exactly how you had things set and restores it once the update lands, so that cleanup work never has to happen twice. Work through the steps below in order; you'll hop over to Vortex between some of them, and your place here is saved while you do.
sync.cardDesc: Shields your Ignored and Disabled choices so an update can't wipe out your setup.

rules-generator.name: The Scribe
rules-generator.heroBody: A Scribe copies a text faithfully, word for word, so nothing is lost in the retelling. Updated to a new collection? Chances are you already spent time getting load-order rules just right in the old one—this tool matches mods between both collections and transcribes those rules straight across, so you're never stuck resolving the exact same conflicts twice. Review every match below before it's committed to Vortex's own record.
rules-generator.cardDesc: Transcribes your proven load-order rules into the updated collection, so you never resolve the same conflicts twice.

update-collection-v2.name: The Herald
update-collection-v2.heroBody: A Herald announces what's coming before it arrives — and carries out what it can. Check your installed collections for news of an update, hear exactly what it changes — removed, updated, and added — and act on the removals and updates for real: real extraction, real deployment, your Ignored and Disabled mods and collection rules carried across untouched.
update-collection-v2.cardDesc: Hear exactly what a collection update changes, then carry out the removals and updates for real.

remove-collection.name: The Quartermaster
remove-collection.heroBody: When a guild or garrison packs up camp, a careless hand might strip the armory bare and leave the rest of the hold defenseless. The Quartermaster inspects every crate before it leaves the gates, checking which provisions are still sworn to your other banners. You decide piece by piece what gets cast aside and what stays behind in the stores, keeping your remaining strongholds completely intact.
remove-collection.cardDesc: Inspects every crate before it leaves — nothing sworn to your other banners goes with it.

report-stats.name: The Ledger
report-stats.heroBody: A Ledger keeps a running tally, so nothing about the accounts is left to memory. Track how every collection you've rebuilt has performed over time, and instantly spot which mods still need attention right now—no more digging through individual run logs one at a time to piece together the full picture.
report-stats.cardDesc: Every rebuild's numbers, tallied over time.

report-workthrough.name: The Quest Log
report-workthrough.heroBody: Every open quest, gathered in one place instead of scattered across a dozen journal entries. This report gathers every problem mod across every collection into one checklist—fix resolvable mismatches and missing archives right here, and check off anything else as you handle it in Vortex yourself. Your progress sticks around until a fresh rerun clears the log.
report-workthrough.cardDesc: Every problem mod left to knock out, in one checklist.

report-updatecompare.name: Scroll of Retrospection
report-updatecompare.heroBody: An Elder Scroll is said to hold past, present, and future all at once. After The Ward finishes its work, this scroll unrolls a clear before-and-after of your mods—what stayed, what got added, and what got removed—so you're never left guessing what an update actually did.
report-updatecompare.cardDesc: Holds your previous setup beside the new one—exactly what was kept, added, or removed.

report-rulesgen.name: The Scribe's Ledger
report-rulesgen.heroBody: Even a Scribe keeps their own record of what's been copied and what's still waiting. See at a glance which mods already have their conflict rules transcribed correctly, and which ones still need a decision or a second look in Vortex—all without re-running the matching process itself.
report-rulesgen.cardDesc: Which rules copied over cleanly, and which still need a look.

report-workshop.name: The Anvil's Mark
report-workshop.heroBody: The painted trade sign out front only tells you when the shop first opened, not when a hammer last fell upon glowing steel—a true armorer looks to the fresh mark stamped into the anvil's own face instead. Nexus's own collection page shows a date that never moves for a private collection; this pulls the real one, straight from each collection's revision history, so you can tell at a glance which ones you've actually worked on recently.
report-workshop.cardDesc: The real date you last set hand to an unfinished work—not Nexus's frozen one.

report-exceptions.name: The Shadowmarked
report-exceptions.heroBody: Carved into doorposts across the cities of Skyrim, a shadowmark conveys an unspoken law to those who know the code: do not pillage, do not interfere, leave this house completely alone. Some mods are hand-pick-only installers where you deliberately chose a subset of what the archive contains—auto-extracting or auto-mending the full archive for one of these doesn't restore what's "missing," it installs content you never chose, which can cause missing masters or crashes. Add a mod here once, and both Restoration and The Vault-Keeper will leave it alone from then on, wherever it shows up.
report-exceptions.cardDesc: Marks the mods you handle yourself—left untouched, wherever they turn up.

missing-masters.name: The Augur
missing-masters.heroBody: An Augur foresees the danger before it arrives, not after. Pinpoint missing master files and instantly see every mod relying on them, all in one clear view—so instead of a sudden crash to desktop, you see the problem coming and can jump straight into Vortex to fix it with confidence.
missing-masters.cardDesc: Reveals a missing master before you launch—no more sudden crash to desktop.

pgpatcher.name: Order of Succession
pgpatcher.heroBody:
When two competing smiths craft enchantments for the exact same armor or blade, only the higher decree determines which design governs your realm. Order of Succession replaces PGPatcher's bare list with full drag-to-reorder, multi-select shifting, and instant A–Z sorting so you can easily establish which mods win your shader conflicts. It reads directly from your existing PGPatcher setup and executes the official PGPatcher engine underneath—generating the identical modrules.json, build files, and logs you rely on, accompanied by real-time build progress every step of the way.

Everything runs on your actual PGPatcher installation. Your existing settings load automatically, and building here runs the genuine PGPatcher engine to produce the exact same final patch and logs—just with a smoother interface and live progress tracking.
pgpatcher.cardDesc: Dictate the chain of command and arbitrate visual precedence across your load order.

scrub.name: The Cleansing
scrub.heroBody: A Cleansing purges what's been left to rot, so nothing lingers past its purpose. Easily spot staging folders and archives that Vortex has quietly stopped tracking—no digging through anything by hand. This shows you exactly what's safe to remove, so you can reclaim disk space with confidence.
scrub.cardDesc: Cleanse the orphaned downloads and abandoned staging folders Vortex left behind, and reclaim the disk space.

archive-finder.name: Clairvoyance
archive-finder.heroBody: Clairvoyance lights the path to what's hidden, without ever having to open the door yourself. Stop extracting archives just to see what's inside—this indexes every zipped mod archive's contents up front, no unpacking needed, so you can instantly search across all of them by file or mod name and pull out exactly the patch you need.
archive-finder.cardDesc: Sees straight through any archive to the exact file you need—without unpacking a single byte.

cycle-helper.name: The Webweaver
cycle-helper.heroBody: A weaver doesn't tear down the whole web to mend one torn thread—she finds the single knotted strand and reweaves just that. When Vortex tangles your load-order rules into a cycle, this finds the one rule actually responsible instead of dumping the whole snarl on you, fixes it, and confirms the web holds.
cycle-helper.cardDesc: One torn thread, mended—not the whole web unraveled.

missing-files.name: The Vault-Keeper
missing-files.heroBody: A vault-keeper fetches the one relic you're missing, not the whole hoard. Whether a collection struck down without the Quartermaster's own inspection cleared out shared relics, a few quietly vanished from your staging folder, or mending the whole collection feels like overkill—this has you covered. It checks the collections you pick, shows exactly what's gone, and restores only what's needed, straight from the archive.
missing-files.cardDesc: Only what's missing, restored—no need to empty the whole vault to replace one relic.

settings.name: The Standing Stones
settings.heroBody: Choose a Standing Stone once, and its blessing shapes your entire journey from then on. Set your Vortex paths and preferences here just once, and every other tool in The Arcaneum picks them up automatically—so you can spend your time on the actual work, not re-entering the same folders over and over.
settings.cardDesc: Choose your paths and preferences once; every tool draws on them.
